requirements.evidence: Most requirements are implemented: migration with cascade FK, nullable invited_by, unique (entity_id,email) (create_entity_invites_table.php:15-23); email normalized in the model (EntityInvite.php:28-41); sendInvite validates, checks for an existing member or pending invite, replaces expired invites, turns a unique violation into an inviteEmail error, queues the mail, writes an audit log and only calls RateLimiter::hit after success (Members.php:66-156); accept/decline check the invitee, handle expiry, are idempotent, avoid duplicate memberships and redirect (PendingInvites.php:286-334); manager-only mount and route middleware (Members.php:61, routes/web.php:874); openMember uses findOrFail before assigning (Members.php:171-173); modals, <hr> only when invites exist, and the lang keys are all there. Gaps: the member modal shows the raw role value instead of the translated one (members.blade.php:803); the e-mail adds an extra untranslated-by-spec 'Thanks,' line; PendingInvites does not handle a guest user in accept/decline (auth()->user()->email on null).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (invite creation, membership creation on accept, invite deletion) stay inline in the Livewire components instead of going through app/Actions/* (Members.php:124-130, PendingInvites.php:309-318). The new properties use inline $this->validate([...]) arrays instead of #[Validate] (Members.php:71-74, 196-198). No tests ship, which breaks the 'no production code without a test' rule. Docs: CHANGELOG is updated (CHANGELOG.md:9), but docs/database-schema.md and docs/business-rules.md are not updated even though the change adds a table and new invariants. Good points: $fillable is set via #[Fillable] (EntityInvite.php:449), the migration has a reversible down(), Bulma modal markup is used.

security.evidence: Every Members action authorizes server-side and resolves IDs through $this->entity->memberships()/invites() (Members.php:162, 171, 182). accept/decline enforce the invitee e-mail match with a 403 (PendingInvites.php:292, 331). The rate limit is checked and hit on the server (Members.php:107-152). Output is escaped with {{ }}. Minor gaps: selectedMembershipId is client-writable and not #[Locked], although saveRole re-scopes it (Members.php:52, 182); PendingInvites resolves any invite globally before the ownership check, so it returns 404 vs 403 and leaks whether an invite ID exists (PendingInvites.php:288).

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all. There are no Pest tests for sendInvite, the rate limit, the race, accept/decline, the 403 paths, the foreign-membership tamper case, the mail rendering or the manager-only route, even though conventions require tests first, including unauthorized-call and tamper tests.

simplicity.evidence: E-mail normalization is done twice, in a saving hook and in a setEmailAttribute mutator (EntityInvite.php:468-481), and again by hand in the components. scopePending() is defined (EntityInvite.php:508) but the same pending query is copied in three places (Members.php:95-99, 248-250, PendingInvites.php:343-344). isPending/isExpired/isAccepted are added but not used. isUniqueViolation does string matching (Members.php:259-266) where Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException exists. The role enum-or-string ternary is repeated across files.

readability.evidence: The code is understandable, but sendInvite is long (~90 lines) and mixes checks, cleanup, insert, mail, logging and throttling. There is repeated inline logic: `$invite->role instanceof \App\Models\UserRole ? ... : ...` appears in the Blade views (members.blade.php:755, 803; pending-invites.blade.php:856; entity-invite.blade.php:665). The mailable keeps generator boilerplate (empty attachments(), `//` constructor). pending-invites.blade.php has no indentation.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: the members component and view, the new invite model, factory, migration, mail and component, the switcher and onboarding includes, the lang files, the route middleware and the CHANGELOG. There are no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests, although the conventions require test-first development with happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action.
Creating invites and creating memberships on accept are domain writes done inline in components instead of in app/Actions/* classes that authorize internally.
Public input properties use inline validate() arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern.
A new table and new membership invariants are added, but the schema and business-rules docs are not updated.
selectedMembershipId is server context but is not #[Locked]; saveRole re-scopes it to the entity, but the policy asks for locking.
Invites are looked up globally and auth()->user() is dereferenced without an auth guard, so a guest call errors and invite-ID existence leaks through 404 vs 403.
E-mail normalization is duplicated (saving hook plus mutator), and the pending scope and helpers are added but the components copy the same query instead of using them.
Unique violations are detected by matching message strings instead of catching Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException.
The member modal shows the raw role value instead of the translated ui.role_* label.
The enum-or-string role ternary is repeated inline in several Blade views; a model accessor or a cast-based ->value would be cleaner.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adds with an invite flow: a migration, model, factory, queued mail, a PendingInvites component, and a manager-only members page with detail and removal modals. Functionally it covers nearly all requirements, with sound server-side authorization and correct rate-limit semantics. It ships no tests at all and keeps domain writes in components instead of Actions, so it needs rework before merging.
